chapter: Tulsa bands, Trent, Holder and Kirk
title: Foots Thomas and the Missourians job he turned down
summary: Walter 'Foots' Thomas, now with the Missourians, offers to get him a fifty-dollar-a-week job, but Fields stays in Tulsa.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well anyway, I'm still not with any band and don't have anything else around there, so the next thing that came up, before it became any band time or anything, Jameson-- I don't remember Jameson's first name. They brought him into the theatre just to play for those silent pictures--a piano player. He would play and get little gigs on the side and that's how Butterbeans and Susie were going on when this Jameson came in. He would get some of the musicians--whenever he would get a little gig--to play with him, and one day, I was on a gig and a youngster came up about my age, and he just stopped and looked funny, up and down; he said, is this Ernest Fields? I said yeah, and it was Walter Thomas--yeah, Foots Thomas. He said, what are you doing? I said, I told you I was going to school, I'm an electrician. He said, I'm a carpenter but I

can play a horn, and I said I can too. So he said we got to get together then and I said yeah. It was in the summertime then, and hot and the wiring, crawling up into the attic on the job and he said, man, I think I can get you something better than this. So I said what. He said I was playing with the Missourians, and they have told me that a guy has brought in (inaudible); an entertainer, a vocalist, that is a terrific showman and they have money behind them, and says they're going to call me. He said will you go if I can get you? I said I'll think about it. He said you better do it, because this is going to be something.

So we would play all around and we would run over to Muskogee sometimes and play a gig and he said you sure got to find out about getting this job. So finally, he would play with this Jameson guy, and I would too, and he finally told Jameson--but he was doing carpenter work--he finally gets his call from way up in Missouri, Kansas and told them to
come, which for that day and time, I think they were guaranteed fifty dollars a week and might have had a chance to make more.

So, he goes and he said when I get down there I'll tell them what kind of fellow you are and I think I can get you in when I get there. He asked them first and they told him to wait, we got it arranged for you now.

As soon as he got there, he called back and said come on, they said all right and I told Jameson and he said well, why don't you wait a while and see how long he's going to get that fifty. Then I said well, if they want to, if they offer that, Jameson couldn't believe it, he thought maybe he wasn't getting it or something, he said let's wait and see; I don't want to hold you back, he says, but Fields, you got to figure it out. He says, you got this job on the side and the people like you and they let you off anytime you want and a lot of times you make more than fifty dollars; and this is
going over there, away from home, and expenses. He said you do whatever you want. So I said, I'll tell you the truth, (inaudible). So anyway, he kept on, Walter talking to Mo and I turned it down--
Fifty dollars a week was riches.
I told Walter that I believe I'll stay on where I was.
Walter went on with the Missourians?
And fifty dollars a week was riches, a lot of money.
